pages.biography_ebrahim_marry_jagana.tex:
Gambian Islamic scholar, educator, preacher, and community
            leader whose lifelong journey has been dedicated to knowledge,
            faith, teaching, and service.

From the Qur'anic learning circles of his village to
                studying at Al-Azhar University in Cairo, Ebrahima Marry
                Jagana's life has been shaped by a deep pursuit of
                knowledge and a commitment to serving Islam and his
                community.

Born in 1966 in New Demba Kunda, The Gambia, Ebrahima
                    Marry Jagana began his journey of learning through the
                    traditional Qur'anic education of his village.

His early studies gave him a foundation in the Qur'an
                    and Islamic knowledge. His desire to deepen that
                    knowledge eventually took him beyond his local
                    community and across the border to Senegal.
A Journey from Village Learning to Al-Azhar

Education remained a defining part of Ebrahima Marry
                    Jagana's life. His pursuit of Islamic knowledge took
                    him through several important stages of study and
                    training.

He began studying the Qur'an and Islamic
                            knowledge through the traditional learning
                            circles of his village.

In 1979, he travelled to neighbouring Senegal
                            to continue his studies in the Islamic
                            sciences and deepen his understanding of
                            religious knowledge.

In 1985, he received a scholarship to study at
                            Al-Azhar University in Cairo, one of the
                            world's historic centres of Islamic learning.

Between 1993 and 1994, he completed his
                            university studies and obtained a licence
                            degree in the Faculty of Education, with a
                            focus on Islamic Studies.

Following university, he undertook additional
                            training in Islamic preaching methods and
                            specialised Arabic-language studies organised
                            through Al-Azhar's Islamic outreach
                            institutions.

For Ebrahima Marry Jagana, the pursuit of knowledge was
                    closely connected to a responsibility to share it.
                    After returning from his educational journey, he began
                    teaching at an Islamic institute associated with the
                    Islamic Union of The Gambia.

From 1995 to 2004, he served in teaching and
                    administrative responsibilities, including work as a
                    secretary in the office of the Director of Education.
                    This period marked an important chapter in his
                    development as an educator and community servant.

In 2004, he moved to the Imam Malik Islamic Institute,
                    where he continued his educational and religious work,
                    serving as a teacher and deputy director of the
                    institute.

His work has extended far beyond formal teaching.
                    Throughout his career, he has served as a preacher,
                    religious guide, imam, and mentor, using different
                    platforms to reach members of his community.

His activities have included preaching, religious
                    education, public guidance, and participation in
                    Islamic committees and community initiatives.

He has also presented a religious programme on national
                    television on a weekly basis for more than fifteen
                    years, extending his educational work to a much wider
                    audience.

Dedicated to teaching Islamic knowledge and
                            supporting the education of students.

Participated in national Islamic committees
                            and community initiatives.

Presented a weekly religious programme on
                            national television for more than 15 years.

Continued religious teaching and guidance
                            through public lessons and community
                            platforms.

Served as an imam and Friday preacher at the
                            Imam Malik Institute mosque.

Shares regular religious lessons through
                            social media and online community groups.

Alongside his teaching and preaching, Ebrahima Marry
                    Jagana has taken part in wider Islamic and community
                    service. His documented activities include
                    responsibilities within national Islamic bodies and
                    committees.

His service has included executive responsibilities in
                    the Higher Islamic Council of The Gambia, including
                    financial responsibilities, as well as participation
                    in national committees concerned with Islamic affairs
                    and the interests of Muslim communities.

He has also contributed to religious education through
                    mosque-based teaching, Friday preaching, and regular
                    lessons shared through social communication platforms.

His profile reflects a combination of religious
                    scholarship, teaching experience, leadership, and
                    communication. He is particularly recognised for his
                    command of the Arabic language and his long-standing
                    involvement in Islamic education and preaching.

His documented skills include strong leadership,
                    excellent Arabic-language ability, and working
                    knowledge of English.
A Life Built Around Knowledge and Service

The story of Ebrahima Marry Jagana is ultimately a story
                    of a lifelong relationship with knowledge. From his
                    earliest Qur'anic studies in New Demba Kunda, through
                    his years of study in Senegal and at Al-Azhar, to his
                    decades of teaching and community service in The
                    Gambia, education has remained at the centre of his
                    journey.

His path illustrates a simple but enduring principle:
                    knowledge becomes most meaningful when it is shared
                    with others and placed in the service of the
                    community.

Through teaching, preaching, leadership, broadcasting,
                    and community engagement, he has continued to make
                    religious knowledge accessible to generations of
                    Gambians.

A lifelong journey of seeking knowledge,
                    sharing knowledge, and serving the community.
Ebrahima Marry Jagana A Life of Knowledge
pages.biography_malamin_zakaria_jagana.t:
A Gambian Islamic scholar, Arabic language teacher, imam, and
            institute director whose journey has carried him from Sierra
            Leone to the Gambia, Egypt, and the United States in pursuit
            of knowledge and service.

Knowledge is light that guides hearts and mends life.
                This is the principle that has carried Malamin Zakaria
                Jagana across three countries and eleven years at
                Al-Azhar University, in a lifelong journey to learn,
                teach, and serve his community.

Malamin Zakaria Jagana was born in 1964 in Kedu Town,
                    in the west of Sierra Leone, to his father Haj
                    Zakaria Jagana and his mother Haja Sisi Kamara. His
                    father worked as a gemstone trader, and it was within
                    this family that his earliest sense of discipline and
                    purpose began to take shape.

While still young, he was sent to live with his uncle,
                    Haj Sheikh Hali Jagana, in the Upper River Region of
                    The Gambia. It was there, until the age of fifteen,
                    that he absorbed the religious and Soninke cultural
                    values that would guide the rest of his life.
From Village Learning to Al-Azhar University

His education followed a long and deliberate path,
                    carrying him through several countries and more than
                    two decades of study before he began his own teaching
                    career.

He memorized the Holy Qur'an at the school of
                            Haj Beely Miala Jagana, laying the foundation
                            for everything that followed.

He travelled to the village of Waoundé to
                            study Islamic jurisprudence under Sheikh Haj
                            Muhammad Sarando Jagana, spending four years
                            deepening his understanding of Islamic law.

He returned briefly to the village, working
                            the groundnut farms before continuing his
                            education the following year.

In early 1985, he travelled to his uncle Haj
                            Mari Haj in Banjul and joined the Fan Afrika
                            school in the village of Lamin, in the West
                            Coast Region.

Later that year, he was awarded a scholarship
                            to Al-Azhar University in Egypt, where he
                            spent eleven years studying Islamic religious
                            sciences, Arabic, English, and French.

He graduated from Al-Azhar University's
                            Faculty of Education, Arabic English
                            Department, with a Good grade bringing his
                            long educational journey to a close.

On returning to The Gambia, Malamin Zakaria Jagana was
                    appointed director of Simoudoughaty School now
                    known as the Imam Malik Islamic Institute under the
                    Simoudoughaty Association, a position he held for
                    four years.

This early leadership role set the tone for a career
                    that would combine classroom teaching with
                    institutional responsibility, a balance he would
                    carry through the rest of his working life.
Seven Years of Teaching and Preaching in Brooklyn

In 2000, he travelled to the United States, where he
                    served as a teacher and preacher at the Abdur Rahman
                    Mosque on Morris Street in Brooklyn, New York, for
                    seven years.

This period placed him at the heart of a Gambian and
                    West African diaspora community, where he continued
                    his work of religious teaching and guidance far from
                    home.

Teaches religious subjects and Arabic language
                            across primary, middle, and secondary levels.

Served as school director and later as
                            institute director for Culture, Dawah,
                            Guidance and Media.

Served as imam and preacher in the Gambia and
                            at Abdur Rahman Mosque in Brooklyn, USA.

Prepares cultural and media programmes for
                            the Imam Malik Islamic Institute.

Works fluently across Soninke, Arabic,
                            English, and French-speaking communities.

Brings decades of organisational and
                            administrative experience to Islamic
                            education.
Back Home at the Imam Malik Islamic Institute

In late 2007, Malamin Zakaria Jagana returned to The
                    Gambia and rejoined the Imam Malik Islamic Institute
                    in Sukuta, where he has remained ever since.

There, he teaches religious and humanities subjects
                    across the primary, middle, and secondary sections,
                    while also serving as the institute's Director of
                    Culture, Dawah, Guidance and Media — a role he has
                    held since the same year.

Together, these two roles reflect the dual nature of
                    his life's work: shaping students in the classroom,
                    and shaping the wider cultural and religious life of
                    the institute and its community.

His documented skills include teaching religious
                    subjects and the Arabic language, school
                    administration and organisational management, dawah,
                    guidance and public speaking, and the preparation of
                    cultural and media programmes.

He is also recognised for his ability to communicate
                    across different cultures — a strength shaped by a
                    life lived between Sierra Leone, The Gambia, Egypt,
                    and the United States, and reflected in his fluency in
                    Soninke, Arabic, English, and French.
A Journey Built on Knowledge and Service

The story of Malamin Zakaria Jagana is one of
                    persistence — a childhood shaped across two countries,
                    years of Qur'anic and fiqh study in village learning
                    circles, and eleven years of formal study at one of
                    the Islamic world's most respected universities.

That foundation has carried into decades of teaching,
                    school leadership, preaching, and cultural guidance
                    first in the Gambia, then in the United States, and
                    now back home again at the Imam Malik Islamic
                    Institute.

Through every stage, his path has reflected the words
                    he holds closest: that knowledge is light, and that
                    its purpose is to guide hearts and mend life.

Knowledge is light that guides hearts and mends
                    life.
Malamin Zakaria Jagana A Life of Knowledge

pages.biography_baguri_kisma_sangare.tex: A Gambian teacher of Arabic language and Islamic studies. Since 2012 at Imam Malik Islamic Institute, he serves as Imam and Khateeb, educator in Arabic and Shari'ah, and presenter on Radio Gambia dedicated to da'wah, education and media outreach.

From the primary school of his village Al-Wanfari to graduating from the International University of Africa, Baguri Kisma Sangare has carried a single conviction: calling to Allah is a responsibility, teaching is a message, and working for Allah is worship.

Born in 1984 in Al-Wanfari, The Gambia, Baguri Kisma Sangare began his education in his village. A Gambian national and family man, he showed early commitment to Arabic and Islamic studies that would lead him beyond his community to higher education.
His academic journey reflects consistent dedication, moving step by step from primary education to university graduation.
Completed his primary stage in his village Al-Wanfari, establishing his foundation in Islamic and general education.
Preparatory Stage — Islamic Institute, Banding Kunja
Joined the Islamic Institute in Banding Kunja and completed his preparatory certificate, deepening his studies in Arabic and Islamic sciences.
Completed his secondary studies, preparing for higher education in Islamic studies.
University Degree — International University of Africa

Enrolled at the International University of Africa, specializing in Islamic Studies. Graduated in 2010 with a university degree in Islamic studies, marking the culmination of his academic journey from village to university.

His qualifications include the primary certificate, preparatory certificate, secondary certificate, and university degree in Islamic Studies each representing a stage of growth from foundational learning to specialized academic training.
Teacher at Imam Malik Islamic Institute, continuously serving since 2012 in Arabic and Islamic studies.
Serves as Imam and Friday preacher, delivering sermons and religious guidance.
Administrator at Imam Malik Institute, Deputy Director of Da'wah and Guidance Affairs, and Secretary of the institute.
Presenter and da'iyah on Radio Gambia (Ida'ah Gambia), extending Islamic education to a national audience.
Member of the Media and Public Relations Committee, managing outreach and communication.
Skilled in computer use, supporting modern educational and administrative work.

His language skills reflect both scholarly training and community roots. Arabic at an excellent level, English very good, Soninke as mother tongue, and Mandinka at an excellent level. This combination allows him to teach and preach across diverse Gambian communities.
Beyond teaching, his experience includes teaching Arabic and Shari'ah sciences, da'wah through radio, and administrative leadership in education and media.

His published research on fiqh, moderation, and the

                    only to studying knowledge, but to recording and

pages.biography_dr_fodi_jagana.text069:
Today, through his work at two universities, an

                    carry that same mission forward: knowledge pursued,
                    lived, and passed on.
pages.biography_dr_fodi_jagana.text070:
Knowledge is worship, acting upon it is a mission,

pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text003: Gambian Islamic scholar, preacher and researcher — PhD in Fiqh from the Islamic University of Madinah — with extensive experience in teaching, research, da'wah and institutional work in The Gambia and Saudi Arabia.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text009: From early Islamic education in The Gambia to earning his Bachelor's, Master's and Doctorate at the Islamic University of Madinah, Dr. Kisma Sheikh Sahoo has dedicated his life to seeking authentic knowledge, teaching it, and serving the community through scholarship and guidance.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text012: Who is Dr. Kisma Sheikh Sahoo?
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text013: Dr. Kisma Sheikh Sahoo is a Gambian scholar of Islamic sciences, a preacher (da'iyah), researcher, and teacher. He originates from Basse area, The Gambia, and holds Gambian nationality.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text014: His profile describes him as an academic with wide scientific and administrative experience in teaching, research, da'wah, and institutional work both in The Gambia and in Saudi Arabia with a clear passion for spreading Islamic knowledge and serving society.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text016: A Journey to the City of the Prophet
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text017: His educational path shows steady progression from foundational Islamic schooling in The Gambia to the highest level of academic study at one of the world's leading Islamic universities.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text019: From the Institute affiliated with the Islamic Union The Gambia, obtaining his primary certificate in Islamic studies.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text021: From the same institute - the Islamic Union Institute, The Gambia - continuing his preparatory level studies.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text023: Completed his secondary Islamic education through the Islamic Union, The Gambia.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text024: Bachelor's in Sharia - Islamic University of Madinah
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text025: Enrolled at the Islamic University of Madinah, Faculty of Sharia, where he obtained his Bachelor's degree in Sharia - a major milestone in his academic journey.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text027: Master's degree from the Islamic University of Madinah, Faculty of Sharia, specializing in Comparative Fiqh. His research focused on Islamic legal theory and comparative jurisprudential issues.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text029: PhD in Fiqh from the Islamic University of Madinah, Faculty of Sharia, specializing in the field of Islamic jurisprudence. His doctoral research addressed contemporary Fiqh issues, reflecting depth in analysis and academic research methodology.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text033: Since 1998, Dr. Sahoo has been active as an imam, preacher, and teacher. His experience includes years of teaching in Islamic schools, preaching in mosques, and serving in educational administration.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text034: His record includes extensive work in da'wah and teaching in The Gambia, supervising research, mentoring students, and participating in Islamic committees. He has also served in roles connected to the Hajj mission (2001-2006 experience as guide/educator for pilgrims) and worked with Islamic institutes for more than 20 years.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text035: Between his studies in Madinah and his work in The Gambia, he has built a profile that combines academic research with practical community education.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text041: Long experience in teaching Islamic sciences at different levels, from primary to advanced.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text044: Active as a preacher and imam, delivering sermons, lessons and religious guidance.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text046: Researcher in Fiqh and comparative Fiqh, with Master's and PhD theses in the field.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text049: Supervising student research and mentoring new teachers and students of knowledge.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text052: Author of research papers and contributions in Islamic jurisprudence.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text055: 15+ years of service (2001-2006) as a guide and educator for Gambian Hajj pilgrims.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text059: Dr. Sahoo is a member of several Islamic bodies. His CV notes membership in the Higher Islamic Council of The Gambia and other scientific and da'wah associations, including roles related to Fatwa and Islamic guidance.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text060: He also collaborates with charitable and educational institutions, combining da'wah with social service, and is known for his involvement in organizing scientific competitions, Qur'an memorization programs (1426-1427 AH), and Islamic awareness activities.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text065: His competencies include strong skills in teaching, research methodology, and community leadership. Linguistically, he is noted for excellent command of Arabic (language of study), proficiency in Soninke as a mother tongue, and good command of English.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text066: These language skills have enabled him to teach diverse audiences and to serve as a bridge between Arab and West African scholarly traditions.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text070: Among his documented achievements: participation in Qur'an and Sunnah competitions in The Gambia, receiving academic distinctions during his studies in Madinah, ranking first in several competitions at the Islamic University, and participation in scholarly conferences and Islamic programs.
pages.biography_dr_kisma_sahoo.text071: His journey from Basse to Madinah and back to serving his community stands as a model of seeking knowledge abroad and returning to benefit one's people.

pages.biography_jaafar_fodi_gumani.text0: Da'iyah • Teacher of Shari'ah • Community Educator

A Gambian da'iyah and teacher of Shari'ah sciences, striving to spread knowledge and da'wah to Allah with wisdom and beautiful preaching, and to build a generation rooted in knowledge, faith, and service to the community.

Since his youth in The Gambia, Jafara Foday Gumaneh has dedicated his life to seeking Islamic knowledge and sharing it. A teacher in Islamic institutes since 1992, he combines traditional learning with decades of practical experience in teaching, preaching, and youth guidance.
A Life Dedicated to Knowledge and Da'wah

Born in 1969 in The Gambia, Jafara Foday Gumaneh began seeking Islamic knowledge at an early age. From 1988 onward, he devoted himself to learning, memorizing, and studying under scholars, before moving into teaching and da'wah.

His vision is clear and consistent: to spread authentic Shari'ah knowledge, invite to Allah with wisdom and good advice, and contribute to building a faithful, educated generation that serves its religion and community through learning, guidance, and good character.
His educational path was built within The Gambia's leading Islamic institutes, combining Shari'ah studies with training in education.
Institute of Islamic Sciences The Gambia
Completed his Shari'ah secondary certificate at the Institute of Islamic Sciences in The Gambia, establishing his foundation in Islamic sciences.
Imam Malik Islamic Institute The Gambia
Obtained a higher diploma in Islamic studies from Imam Malik Islamic Institute, deepening his studies in Qur'an, Hadith, Fiqh and Seerah.
Completed a specialized diploma combining Shari'ah and Islamic education methodology, preparing him for teaching and curriculum development.
More Than Three Decades of Teaching
Since 1992, Jafara Foday Gumaneh has been a teacher in Islamic institutes and schools, a period spanning over 30 years of continuous educational service.
Teaching Qur'an al-Kareem, Hadith, Fiqh, and Seerah in institutes and schools.
Serving as Imam and Friday preacher for many years, guiding worshippers through sermons and lessons.
Active participation in da'wah programs, awareness campaigns, and community education.
Supervising halaqas for Qur'an memorization and mentoring youth and students of knowledge.
Commitment to continuous learning has remained central to his work, with specialized training across core Islamic disciplines.
Advanced courses in Qur'anic exegesis and Qur'anic sciences.
Specialized studies in Hadith sciences and its terminology.
Studies in Fiqh and Usul al-Fiqh, principles and applications.
Training in da'wah methodology, preaching skills, and community outreach.
Over 30 years explaining Shari'ah sciences with clarity and sincerity.
Known for effective khutbah, public speaking, and da'wah with wisdom.
Providing religious guidance and mentorship to youth and families.
Preparing curricula, managing study circles, and organizing educational programs.
Organizing programs for youth and children, Qur'an competitions and da'wah campaigns.
Strong interpersonal communication and effective use of modern tools in teaching.

Fluent in Soninke as a mother tongue, with strong command of Mandinka, very good Arabic (read), good English, and good Mandinka allowing him to teach and preach across different communities in The Gambia.

He is recognized for personal qualities that define an educator: commitment, discipline, sincerity, love for knowledge and teaching, perseverance in work, team spirit, and dedication to collective effort.

His mission centers on spreading authentic Shari'ah knowledge, nurturing students who adhere to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah, and building generations that benefit the Ummah. A vision pursued through teaching, da'wah, guidance, and dedicated community service.
Spreading Shari'ah knowledge and calling to Allah with wisdom and beautiful preaching Jafara Foday Gumaneh
pages.biography_muhammad_issa_haydar.tex: Master's in Education • Curriculum Developer • Educator

A Gambian educator and specialist in Arabic language education, with a Master's in Education. Serving as Arabic language teacher at Imam Malik Institute since 2004, Director of Educational Affairs, and active Imam and Khateeb.

From early studies in Mali to higher education in Sudan, and over two decades of teaching Arabic in The Gambia, Muhammad Issa Haydara represents a journey of dedication to education, curriculum development, and community guidance.

Born on 28 August 1972 in Masra - Mariam, The Gambia, Muhammad Issa Haydara is a Gambian national whose life has been centered on education. Married and residing in Masra - Mariam, he has built his career around teaching Arabic, guiding students, and improving educational standards.
His focus has always been practical and impactful: preparing curricula, managing educational affairs, and standing on the minbar to guide the community.
A Path Through Mali and Sudan
His academic formation took him across the region, from traditional foundational learning to specialized university training in Arabic language education.
Completed his primary and preparatory education in Mali, establishing a strong foundation in Arabic and Islamic studies.
Continued his secondary and university studies in Sudan, specializing in Education, Arabic Language Department, where he developed expertise in teaching methodology and Arabic linguistics.
Obtained a Master's degree in Education, specializing in Arabic Language, combining pedagogical theory with linguistic specialization.

His linguistic profile reflects both his heritage and his professional specialization. Soninke is his mother tongue. Arabic is at an excellent level, the language of his teaching and research. French is also excellent. English is very good, in addition to knowledge of several local Gambian languages.
This multilingual capacity enables him to teach diverse student populations and contribute to curriculum development that serves a wide community.
Specialist in preparing and developing academic curricula for Arabic and Islamic education.
Responsible for managing and overseeing educational affairs and academic quality.
Arabic language teacher at Imam Malik Institute, serving continuously from 2004 to the present.
Active Imam and Friday preacher, delivering regular sermons and religious lessons.
Member of the Examinations Committee under the General Secretariat for Arabic and Islamic Studies in The Gambia.
Previously and currently a member of the national curriculum committee for Arabic and Islamic education.

Since 2004, his work at Imam Malik Institute has shaped generations of students. Through classroom teaching, administrative leadership, curriculum design, and minbar guidance, he has contributed to raising the standard of Arabic language education in The Gambia.

His role in national examination and curriculum committees reflects a commitment that goes beyond a single institute working to improve the quality of Arabic and Islamic education at a national level.
Preparing curricula and serving Arabic and Islamic education Muhammad Issa Haydara

Born 10 Feb 1987
Demba Kunda, The Gambia
Master's Degree 2014/2015
Qur'an Teacher Since 2001

The story of Muhammad Jola Camara begins in Demba Kunda and extends to the universities of Sudan a journey driven by a single purpose: to serve the Book of Allah through learning, teaching, and building faithful Qur'anic generations.
His Original Biography
Beginnings
From Demba Kunda to the Qur'an

Born on 10 February 1987 in Demba Kunda, The Gambia, Muhammad Jola Camara began his educational journey in his village at the school of the Salafi Islamic Association. His early inclination toward the Qur'an led him to the Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah Qur'anic School in Bantan, where he studied under Sheikh Ahmad Somali.
In 2001, he completed the memorization of the Holy Qur'an a foundational achievement that shaped his entire future path as a teacher and educator.
Academic Journey
An Academic Path to Sudan

After completing his Hifz, he joined the Islamic Institute in Banjul, completing his preparatory and secondary studies in the academic year 2006/2007. Seeking higher Islamic education, he traveled to Sudan.
Hifz al-Qur'an Sheikh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah School
Certificate of memorization of the Holy Qur'an, with proficiency and Tajweed, under the supervision of Sheikh Ahmad Somali.
Secondary Certificate Islamic Institute

Teaching has been at the center of his life since his youth, moving from mosque circles to institutes and international schools.
Teacher of Qur'an Halaqah Old Demba Kunda Mosque

Teacher of Qur'an and Tajweed Imam Malik Institute
Joined Imam Malik Islamic Institute as a teacher of the Holy Qur'an and Tajweed, contributing to its Qur'an program.
Teacher of Qur'an Sudanese Schools, Sudan
During his postgraduate studies, taught the Holy Qur'an in Sudanese schools in Sudan, gaining international teaching experience.
Imamah
Imam Dar al-Hadith Center
Served as Imam at Dar al-Hadith Center, Ndum, leading prayers and providing religious guidance.
Present
Senior Teacher

Currently a senior participant at Imam Malik Institute, specializing in teaching Qur'anic subjects including Tafsir and Tajweed, and also serving in financial administration of the institute.

Tajweed
Qira'at
Expert in Tajweed rules and Qur'anic recitation, with years of practical teaching.
Educational Administration
Experienced in managing educational programs and academic affairs.

Contributing to the financial administration of Imam Malik Institute.

Certified in basic computer applications, supporting modern educational work.

Skilled in preparing scientific programs and educational courses for students.
Languages
Mission
Serving the Book of Allah
Fluent in Arabic, English, Soninke, and Mandinka, he is able to teach and communicate across The Gambia's diverse communities.

His mission is clear: to strive in serving the Book of Allah, to spread beneficial knowledge, and to contribute to building faithful Qur'anic generations. A mission he continues to fulfill at Imam Malik Institute with dedication and trust in Allah.

A Gambian teacher of Arabic language and Islamic studies with long experience in teaching and administration. From the Kuttab of Drami family to a degree in Arabic and Islamic Studies, he has taught at Imam Malik Institute since 2007 and continues his mission in education and student development.

From learning the basics of reading in the Kuttab of the Drami family to leading examinations and student affairs at Imam Malik Institute, Muhammad Kaowjed Camara has dedicated his life to teaching, nurturing student confidence, and organizing educational life with discipline and care.

Born in Dimanaka Qadima, Yassi District, Republic of The Gambia, Muhammad Kaowjed Camara began his educational journey before 1991 in the Kuttab of Al Drami in Baghrini, under the tutelage of Sheikh Al-Hajj Bakr Drami may Allah preserve him where he learned the principles of reading and foundational Islamic knowledge.
This traditional beginning instilled in him a love for learning and teaching that would shape his entire career.
A Path From Kuttab to University
Started his learning in the Kuttab of Al Drami, under Sheikh Al-Hajj Bakr Drami, where he learned the basics of reading and Qur'anic principles.
Salafi Association School Sheikh Mahmoud Sissi Camara Village

Joined the school of the Salafi Association in 1991 in the village of Sheikh Mahmoud Sissi Camara — may Allah have mercy on him. Studied Fiqh and all Islamic sciences, completing his primary stage in 2000.
Moved to Serekunda and enrolled at the Islamic Union Institute (Landil King). Studied the preparatory and secondary stages from 2000 to 2007, successfully completing his secondary education.
College of Islamic Da'wah Senegal Branch
In 2011, he gained admission to the College of Islamic Da'wah — Senegal Branch. Graduated in 2015 with a Bachelor's degree (Licence) in Arabic Language and Islamic Studies.
His teaching career began immediately after his secondary graduation and has continued without interruption.
Appointed as a teacher at Imam Malik Islamic Institute after graduating from the secondary stage, serving from 2007 to 2011.
After graduating from university, he returned to The Gambia and resumed teaching at Imam Malik Islamic Institute since 2015, continuing his message in education and serving students of knowledge.
Teaching linguistic and Islamic studies subjects at different academic stages at Imam Malik Institute.

Established a student affairs committee to develop the institute and provide diverse student activities, focusing on training students to speak at the morning assembly to build self-confidence and eloquence.
Preparing a monthly schedule for distributing teachers to supervise morning students and organizing daily educational life.
Serving as Director of Examinations at Imam Malik Islamic Institute, managing academic evaluation.
Internal monitor overseeing academic discipline, attendance and quality.
Assistant for inspection works and assistant in organizing workflow at Imam Malik Institute.

His approach combines classroom teaching with student development and administrative precision. Whether forming a committee for student affairs, training students to stand confidently before their peers, or organizing teacher supervision schedules, his work reflects a belief that education is both knowledge and character.
Since 2015, he has continued this mission at Imam Malik, dedicating his efforts to teaching and to serving students of knowledge.
My mission continues in teaching and serving students of knowledge Muhammad Kaowjed Camara
pages.biography_muhammad_muhammad_touray: A Gambian educator, preacher and orator dedicated to teaching, guidance and community service. A graduate of Al-Azhar Al-Sharif, serving as teacher and Head of the English Department at Imam Malik Institute and as Imam and Khateeb of Abu al-Khair Mosque, Sukuta.

From the Qur'anic learning circles of Gamibisara to the lecture halls of Al-Azhar in Cairo, the path of Muhammad Muhammad Touray has been shaped by a lifelong commitment to learning the religion and teaching it in the classroom, on the minbar, and through the airwaves.

Born on 10 October 1973 in Koinya Kantora, The Gambia, Muhammad Muhammad Touray grew up in a family rooted in faith son of Muhammad Touray and Hajja Fatima Mama Omani. His early education began in the traditional majlis of the late Al-Haj Babou Fouti in Gamibisara, where he built his foundation in Qur'an and Islamic sciences.
That early grounding sparked a desire to seek knowledge beyond his village, taking him to renowned centers of learning across West Africa and to Egypt.
His pursuit of knowledge reflects the classic path of West African scholars moving between local scholars, specialized institutes, and university education.
Began his studies in the council of the late Al-Haj Babou Fouti in the village of Gamibisara, learning Qur'an and foundational Islamic sciences.
Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith Tuba, Mali
Traveled to Tuba, Mali to study at Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith, deepening his knowledge in Qur'anic and Hadith sciences.
Institute of Islamic Research Cairo, Egypt
Joined the Islamic Research Institute (Ma'had al-Buhuth al-Islamiyya) in Cairo, affiliated with Al-Azhar, where he completed his secondary education with a very good grade.
Al-Azhar University Faculty of Education, English Department

Admitted to the prestigious Al-Azhar University in Cairo, Faculty of Education, English Department. He obtained his Licence (Bachelor's degree) with a good grade, combining Islamic education with strong English language training.

His academic record shows consistent excellence: a primary certificate with excellent honors from Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith, a secondary certificate with very good honors from the Al-Azhar Islamic Research Institute, and a university licence from Al-Azhar University's Faculty of Education.
This combination of traditional grounding and modern university training gave him the ability to teach in both Arabic and English, and to connect with diverse audiences.
Teacher and member of the administrative board at Imam Malik Institute for Islamic Education.
Leads the English Department at Imam Malik Institute, bridging Islamic knowledge and English education.
Imam and Friday preacher at Abu al-Khair Mosque, Sukuta Serekunda, guiding the community through sermons and lessons.
Regular preacher and advisor on Unique FM, extending religious guidance to a wider audience through media.
Muhammad Muhammad Touray is known for his strong communication skills and ability to reach people across linguistic communities in The Gambia.

His mother tongue is Soninke, alongside fluency in Mandinka and Wolof. In Arabic, he has very good command in both speaking and writing the language of his advanced studies. In English, the official language of The Gambia, he is also highly proficient in speaking and writing, a result of his specialization at Al-Azhar.
This multilingual ability, combined with years of experience in teaching, administration, da'wah, and khutbah, has made him a trusted teacher, orator, and guide in his community.
My Lord, increase me in knowledge and grant me understanding Muhammad Muhammad Touray
pages.biography_musa_muhammad_jibo.text0: Islamic University of Madinah • Student Affairs • Qur'an Center

A Gambian educator and administrator. Graduate of the Islamic University of Madinah in 2014, he serves as Deputy Director of Student Affairs at Imam Malik Islamic Institute and Head of the Supreme Committee at the Center for Qur'an Memorization and Islamic Studies.

From secondary studies at Ma'had al-Nour al-Islami in 2008 to graduating from the Islamic University of Madinah in 2014, Musa Muhammad Jibo has combined academic excellence with dedicated service to student development and Qur'an education in The Gambia.
From Basse to the City of the Prophet
Completed his secondary certificate at Ma'had al-Nour al-Islami in 2008, building a strong foundation in Islamic sciences and Arabic language.
Bachelor's Degree Islamic University of Madinah

Admitted to the Islamic University of Madinah al-Munawwarah, one of the world's most prestigious centers for Islamic learning. Graduated in 2014 with a Bachelor's degree, returning to The Gambia to serve in Islamic education.

During his time in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, he participated in six specialized training programs in 1435-1436 AH, reflecting a commitment to student development, intellectual awareness, and educational excellence.
Training program focused on Zakat education and community awareness, held in Saudi Arabia.
Qualification and Training of Distinguished Students 1435 AH
Program dedicated to nurturing and training outstanding students.
Human Chain Initiative to Reject Terrorism 1435 AH

Professional development project for graduating students, focusing on career readiness.
Course addressing intellectual challenges and their remedies, emphasizing critical thinking and authentic knowledge.
Specialized course in the sciences of the Prophetic Sunnah and its preservation.
At Imam Malik Islamic Institute, overseeing student welfare, discipline, and development programs.
At the Center for Tahfiz al-Qur'an al-Karim and Islamic Studies, leading strategic planning and academic oversight.
Trained in programs for distinguished students and graduate qualification, focused on building confident, capable students.
Engaged in initiatives promoting peace, rejecting terrorism, and addressing intellectual challenges facing youth.

His linguistic and personal skills support his educational leadership. Arabic at an excellent level the language of his university studies in Madinah. English at an intermediate level. Fluent in Soninke and Mandinka, connecting with diverse communities across The Gambia.

His training in student affairs, Sunnah studies, and intellectual awareness, combined with his administrative roles, positions him as an educator who cares for both academic knowledge and character building.
From Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah to serving the Book of Allah in The Gambia Musa Muhammad Jibo
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text00: Educator • Qur'an Memorization Specialist • Da'wah Supervisor

An educator and specialist in Qur'an memorization and Islamic education. From traditional learning in Sierra Leone to leading educational roles at Imam Malik Institute in The Gambia since 2001, his life has been dedicated to teaching the Qur'an and serving da'wah.

The journey of Omar Issa Dukureh bridges two West African nations and over three decades of service to the Qur'an. From memorizing the Book of Allah to supervising its memorization for generations of students, his path is one of dedication to education and da'wah.
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text01: From Sierra Leone to The Gambia

Omar Issa Dukureh was born in 1972 in the Republic of Sierra Leone, West Africa, and holds Gambian nationality. Belonging to the Dukureh family, he received his early traditional education in Sierra Leone before his educational journey brought him to The Gambia, where he has since built his life of service.
His formation combines traditional West African Islamic learning with formal Islamic education, centered on the Qur'an and its sciences.
Learning, Memorizing, and Teaching the Qur'an
His educational path reflects a lifelong relationship with the Holy Qur'an — as a student, memorizer, and later as a teacher and supervisor.
Received his traditional Islamic education in Sierra Leone, building a foundation in Qur'an and basic Islamic sciences.
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text02: Completed his primary and preparatory (intermediate) studies at Dar al-Qur'an and Hadith, focusing on Qur'an memorization and Hadith sciences.
In 1984, he joined the Qur'an memorization department. He devoted himself to memorizing the Holy Qur'an, completing his memorization and receiving recognition for his efforts.
Completed the memorization of the entire Qur'an in 1988, marking a major milestone that would define his future service in Qur'an education.
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text03: Obtained his intermediate and secondary qualifications in The Gambia between 1992 and 1996, followed by higher studies. In 2001, he completed advanced studies in Shari'ah and Islamic education, with focus on Qur'an sciences and teaching methodology.
Leading Qur'an Education at Imam Malik Institute
Since 2001, Omar Issa Dukureh has held a series of key educational, administrative and da'wah responsibilities, particularly at Imam Malik Institute.
First Director Imam Malik Islamic Institute, Serekunda
Served as the first Director of Imam Malik Islamic Institute in Serekunda, establishing its early educational programs and administrative structure.
Served as Deputy Director of the institute, supporting academic planning and daily administration.
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text04: Supervisor of the Qur'an memorization department, overseeing halaqas, memorization programs, and student progress.
Deputy Director for Educational Affairs, responsible for academic quality, curriculum implementation, and teacher coordination.
Supervisor of Da'wah Program — Sheikh Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Sheikh
Supervisor of the da'wah program affiliated with Sheikh Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Sheikh in The Gambia, coordinating Islamic awareness and outreach activities.
Service to the Qur'an and Community
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text05: First Director and later Deputy Director of Imam Malik Institute, shaping its growth since 2001.
Supervisor of Qur'an memorization, guiding students in Hifz and Tajweed.
Deputy for educational affairs, managing academic programs and standards.
Supervisor of national da'wah programs, extending education beyond the classroom.
Participant in national Qur'an memorization competitions, including events in 2006 and 2008.
pages.biography_omar_issa_dukureh.text06: Long-standing service in teaching, mosque activities, and community education.

Fluent in multiple languages reflecting his cross-cultural journey: Arabic, English, Soninke, Mandinka, Malinke, and Krio (Sierra Leonean). This linguistic diversity enables him to connect with students and communities across The Gambia and Sierra Leone.
His work is marked by dedication to the Qur'an, commitment to education, and a focus on building strong memorization programs that preserve the Book of Allah for future generations.

pages.index.text035: Al-Imam Malick Islamic Institute Gift to the World
pages.index.text036: A leading Islamic educational institution in The Gambia, dedicated to knowledge, discipline, and community service.
pages.index.text038: Rooted in the teachings of Imam Malik, the institute offers disciplined Islamic education through both its Tahfiz and Madrasa programs, providing strong moral guidance and a learning environment that shapes confident, value‑driven students.
pages.index.text040: Where Islamic Sharia studies and scientific
pages.index.text041: disciplines come together under one roof.
pages.index.text043: Imam Malick Islamic Institute welcomes students from diverse backgrounds across The Gambia and West Africa, creating a rich environment of shared languages, cultures, and Islamic values.
pages.index.text045: Imam Malick Islamic Institute provides students with access to essential Islamic texts, learning resources, and a supportive environment that strengthens both academic growth and cultural understanding.
pages.index.text046: Why Choose Imam Malick Islamic Institute?
pages.index.text047: Rooted in the teachings of Imam Malik, the institute offers disciplined Islamic education through its Tahfiz program and Islamic School program, providing strong moral guidance and a learning environment that shapes confident, value‑driven students.
pages.index.text050: Al‑Imam Malick Islamic Institute upholds strong academic and Islamic standards across all levels Elementary, Preparatory, and High School. The institute follows the Maliki school of jurisprudence and maintains a curriculum aligned with national education guidelines in The Gambia, ensuring quality Islamic and academic learning.
pages.index.text052: The institute welcomes students from across The Gambia and West Africa, creating a vibrant environment enriched with multiple languages, cultures, and shared Islamic values. This diversity strengthens unity, brotherhood, and mutual respect among students.
pages.index.text054: Al‑Imam Malick Islamic Institute supports families by offering accessible education, including scholarship opportunities for outstanding students and those in need. These scholarships help students pursue Islamic studies and academic excellence without financial barriers.
pages.index.text056: Al‑Imam Malick Islamic Institute is located in a peaceful community within The Gambia, providing students with an environment that supports Islamic learning, discipline, and academic growth. The institute serves families across the region and stands as a center of knowledge rooted in the Maliki tradition.

pages.school_history_index.text007: The Official History of Imam Malik Islamic Institute
pages.school_history_index.text008: The history of the institute begins with the founding of Samboudoukati Association in 1960. Its first headquarters was located in Banjul, in the house of Alhaji Musa Njai (may Allah have mercy on him) at 16 Lemon Street. When the place became too small, the association moved to the house of Alhaji Saibo Tankara on Lancaster Street.
pages.school_history_index.text009: Education began in the traditional kuttab (Qur’anic school) style, with students attending morning and evening sessions.
pages.school_history_index.text010: The teachers during this early period were:
pages.school_history_index.text011: Sheikhba Sise (may Allah have mercy on him), the son‑in‑law of Alhaji Baba Kamara.
pages.school_history_index.text012: Alhaji Baba Kamara (may Allah have mercy on him).
pages.school_history_index.text013: Jindi Simiga Jani (may Allah have mercy on him).
pages.school_history_index.text014: In 1996, the institute shifted from the traditional kuttab system to a formal academic system. The teachers at that time were:
pages.school_history_index.text016: Ousman Muhammad Samba Drammeh – Deputy Director
pages.school_history_index.text019: The primary stage (Grades 1–3) was opened in Banjul and continued until the year 2000. At that time, the institute was known as “Samboudoukati Islamic School”.
pages.school_history_index.text020: In 2001, the association opened a new school in Kanifing, starting with Grade 5. Its name was:
pages.school_history_index.text021: “The Islamic School for Qur’an Memorization and the Study of Islamic and Modern Sciences – Samboudoukati Association – Kanifing”.
pages.school_history_index.text025: Later, the school in Banjul — along with its students and teachers — moved to Kanifing, led by the Deputy Director Ustaz Ousman Muhammad Samba Drammeh, after Director Malamin Jagna traveled to the United States. Drammeh then assumed full responsibility for managing the school.
pages.school_history_index.text026: By 2002, the school had reached Grade 6. In 2003, the junior secondary level was opened. The first graduating class completed their studies in 2008/2009, consisting of eight male students.
pages.school_history_index.text027: The institute witnessed significant growth with the arrival of two teachers in October 2004:
pages.school_history_index.text028: Ustaz Muhammad Kaba Musa (may Allah have mercy on him)
pages.school_history_index.text033: In 2005, the name of the institute was officially changed to:
pages.school_history_index.text035: based on a suggestion from Dr. Fodi Baba Jagna while he was a student at the Islamic University in Madinah.
